title: [30/9/2023] The percentages of Chinese and Indian students in Canadian universities
prompt: The chart shows the percentages of Chinese and Indian students in Canadian universities in various provinces in 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart lists the percentages of Chinese and Indian students who were attending universities in 9 different provinces of Canada in 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Chinese students outnumbered their Indian counterparts in all the given provinces, with the exception of Alberta. In addition, the figures for New Brunswick were the largest in terms of both Chinese and Indian students, while no students from India chose P.E.I. as their place of study.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most popular destinations, New Brunswick took the lead, as it was comprised of roughly 12% and 7% Chinese and Indian nationals, respectively. A similar percentage of around 10.5% was seen in the figures for Chinese students in both Nova Scotia and British Columbia, while Indian students, in turn, accounted for just approximately 6.3% and 4.4%. Meanwhile, Quebec reported that slightly over 8% of their students were Chinese, which was about 2% higher than Indian citizens.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining provinces, in Alberta alone, students from India surpassed those from China, at approximately 5.5% and just above 4%, respectively. Additionally, the numbers of Chinese students in Yukon, Manitoba and Ontario ranged from slightly above 7.5% to as low as 6%, while Indian attendees came in at roughly 2.5% lower in all three provinces. Finally, Prince Edward Island was the only province with no reported students coming from India, although there remained slightly under 5% who were Chinese.
